subject: Quantitative MAP: token assumptions & benchmarking for Acme Health pilot
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Klein <jordan.k@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quantitative MAP: token assumptions & benchmarking for Acme Health pilot

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, the next step for the mutual action plan (MAP) is to lock in the unit-economics assumptions so we can price the pilot and size Dedicated capacity if you move forward. I pulled together a short checklist we need from your side and a few Redwood assumptions that will affect the tokens/$ math. Please skim and reply with the bold items below so we can finalize the MAP deliverable this week.

ACME -> please confirm:
- Expected monthly active users (MAU) or API calls: bold the best estimate.
- Typical session pattern: average turns per session and whether sessions have long context (e.g., multi-turn threads with >2k tokens).
- Percent of templated/static prompts (eligible for prefix/KV caching).
- Latency SLO (p50/p95) and whether 300–500ms tail is acceptable for the pilot.

Redwood assumptions (please flag anything off):
- Avg prompt tokens: 120 tokens; avg model response: 380 tokens (500 total).
- Cacheable fraction (conservative): 25% hit rate on prompts where KV/prefix caching applies; optimistic: 40%.
- Batching target for Dedicated pilot: effective batch size ~6–8 requests to balance latency vs cost (we can tune).
- Quantization: we’ll test FP16 and 8-bit quant variants; expected cost win ~20–35% on token compute depending on quality requirements.

Deliverables we’ll produce for MAP:
- Filled cost workbook (template attached) with tokens/$ and per-user/month cost at low/median/high adoption.
- A small benchmark run (internal) matching your prompt mix to validate avg tokens & throughput.
- Timeline and gating: bench -> pilot pricing proposal -> procurement terms/PO.

If you can reply with the MAU estimate and session profile today, Marissa will run a quick sensitivity model and send a conservative per-seat cost for procurement.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales (West) | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: IR-ACME-cost-template-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
From: Jordan Klein <jordan.k@acmehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantitative MAP: token assumptions & benchmarking for Acme Health pilot

Hi Irene —

Thanks — see rough traffic assumptions below, happy to refine. Procurement is looped for visibility.

- Expected pilot user base: 5,000 monthly active users; target expansion to 25k MAU in 6 months.
- Average session: 3.6 turns (user prompt + assistant responses), typical prompt size ~100–140 tokens, avg assistant reply ~320–420 tokens depending on content (so ~420–560 total tokens per request).
- Template/structured prompts (forms, standard follow-ups): ~35% of calls are highly similar and likely cacheable.
- Concurrency: peak QPS around 8–12 for the pilot; sustained throughput lower (~2–4 QPS typical).
- Latency: p95 target <800ms for pilot; p50 can be lower.

We also have a small compliance ask: logs retention for 90 days and audit access for SOC docs during procurement.

Jordan
Jordan Klein | Dir. Product, Acme Health
jordan.k@acmehealth.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Klein <jordan.k@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:48:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quantitative MAP: token assumptions & benchmarking for Acme Health pilot

Looping in my quick read of Jordan’s numbers and proposed conservative MAP assumptions. I ran a brief sensitivity pass against the attached workbook — highlights below.

Key model points (conservative / realistic / optimistic):
- Tokens per call: 520 / 490 / 420 (we should use 520 for procurement pricing to avoid undercommitment).
- Cacheable fraction: 25% / 35% / 45% (Jordan suggested ~35% - I'll model 25% in the conservative sheet).
- Batching: For Dedicated pilot we recommend initial batch window 30ms with target effective batch size = 5 to 7. That keeps p95 latency ~350–650ms depending on model variant; if Acme needs tighter tails we can reduce batch window at cost of ~12–18% higher per-token compute cost.
- Quantization: Test w/8-bit (Q8) on the pilot model; expect ~22% cost reduction vs FP16 in typical throughput scenarios. We’ll include a quality guardrail test.

Preliminary per-1M-requests cost (conservative assumptions): compute + infra = $X* (placeholder in sheet) — final numbers after benchmark run.

Proposed MAP milestones and dates:
1) Today (4/19): Acme confirms MAU and caching guidance (Jordan).
2) 4/21: Redwood runs a 2-hour synthetic benchmark using Acme prompt mix and returns measured tokens, latency p50/p95, and effective cache hit.
3) 4/23: Redwood sends pilot pricing sheet + recommended Dedicated sizing + optional fallback hosted SLA.
4) 4/30: Target procurement PO or decision to extend trial.

Open questions for procurement: acceptable PO lead time and whether Acme needs an invoicing milestone schedule. Jordan/procurement, can you share preferred PO cadence?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachment referenced: token_econ_snapshot.pdf (pdf, 85KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantitative MAP: token assumptions & benchmarking for Acme Health pilot

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the quick response. We’ll run the benchmark on 4/21 as Marissa outlined and send the filled workbook and the recommended pricing by 4/23.

Summary / next steps for the MAP (finalized):
- Redwood action: 4/21 benchmark (Marissa) -> deliver p50/p95, measured avg tokens, effective cache hits.
- Redwood deliver: 4/23 pricing workbook (IR-ACME-cost-template-v1.xlsx updated) + Dedicated sizing recommendation.
- Acme action: confirm PO cadence and any procurement constraints by 4/26; if PO not possible, confirm whether a 30-day pilot invoice is acceptable.

I’ve attached the cost workbook and included a short summary sheet for procurement. If procurement needs a separate SOW/statement, Ben can draft a light SOW once we have final numbers.

Irene
